One entry per PR. `lane` is the cloud fixer thread that owns the PR's files; lanes own disjoint file sets, and a PR that must edit another lane's file lists it under Borrowed in its brief and carries an `after` edge on that lane's last PR on it.
`wave` is the dependency depth (1 = startable now). `owner_gate` names why tvofi must approve; those PRs are kept apart so nothing else waits on them.

`model` routes each role (tvofi 19:05Z): the fixer to the cheapest feasible model with the reason when it is the strongest, reviews and RCA to opus, runners to haiku, record upkeep to sonnet. `resume` names the branch, the resume note on it, and how a cloud or a Mac seat picks the PR up (FIX-PLAN.md sections 11 and 12).

`issues` lists the Phase E class issues (#1644-#1688; #1689 closed as not planned with D8-s2-01) each PR's findings, instances, barrier or covers belong to, and `fixes` the ones it closes, because it follows every other PR holding that class; the body says Fixes #N for those and Part of #N for the rest. `sweep_instances` names the Phase D instances each PR carries beyond its findings (FIX-PLAN.md's instance table). groups.brief: Round-9 fix PR F6.3 (Dashboard card lane). Models: fixer opus (a class barrier carrying an RCA prototype (P9, +572 lines of browser harness)); reviewer opus in another session; RCA and judge opus; runner work (scoped-gate and stress re-runs, closure and budget re-records, report rendering) goes to a haiku subagent that reports numbers and decides nothing; record upkeep (resume note, RESUME.md line, delivery row) may go to sonnet. Class barrier landing here: P9 (RCA seat reported, process state (c)). Form: a property-keyed grid inside tests/card_browser.mjs: 31 states by 7 cells, WCAG AA contrast composited over what is underneath, zero shared glyph ink between text runs, pop-ups inside viewport and chart, distinct options, no unreachable clipped ink, 24 px targets or the 2.5.8 spacing exception; controls: every cell mounted and every driver step found, and reach (every colour-setting CSS rule matches a visible element in some cell). Reduced motion, frozen clock. Prototype handoff/r9-rca-p9@4f3b9d4f; cherry-pick 4f3b9d4f (tests/card_browser.mjs +572). Lines: 0 production; +572 test, some of which the fixer may pay back by deleting per-instance witnesses the grid subsumes. Ownership: code-owned (tests/card_browser.mjs); no policy file. Demonstrate it failing on each round-9 instance re-introduced, passing on the fixed tree, and silent on a healthy tree, as the RCA's own runs did; set the class's entry in tools/audit/bugclasses.json (detector, barrier, status) in this PR. The P9 class barrier (below), after F6.1 (which carries all four of the RCA's instances since tvofi's D2 answer): the grid is a zero rule with no allow-list (fixer.md step 14), so it merges green only once every judged instance and the RCA's four are fixed or dispositioned. Scope (orchestrator's ruling on the RCA's cost question, 2026-09-26): the grid's cost (about 134 s per browser run as measured) is scoped to card-surface diffs through the scoped gate, with main forced full. The lane is not scoped today (NOT_A_TEST, runs on every PR): implement the scoping so the lane prints which mode it ran, a skip is never read as a pass, and a push to main runs it; a change to .github/workflows/tests.yml is F11's and code-owned, so hand that part back rather than borrow it. The fixer may pay lines back by deleting per-instance witnesses the grid subsumes (the REQUIRED four-selector contrast loop is the obvious one), each only after showing the grid failing on that witness's own perturbation. The grid is not a keyboard lane: the 204 pointer-only hits stay F6.2's to re-check with keyboard cells on. Also catches F6.2's two extra P9 instances (orchestrator, 2026-09-26: a new overlapping label and pointer-only hit targets, both found by F6.1): the barrier is a zero rule, so it merges green only once those two, like the RCA's four, are fixed or dispositioned in F6.2. P9-f61c is the second tap-target-growth candidate, beside P9-rca4, and lands here rather than F6.2 (orchestrator, 2026-09-27): like P9-rca4 it needs a fix design, not a re-measure -- grow each slot target against its neighbours' grown targets, not their ink, or disposition it with the measurement. One attempt (half-gap growth) made 53 targets worse, so show the whole grid's target count at both ends (merge base and head) for both candidates. Forward-carry provenance (finding-propagation.md; orchestrator, 2026-09-27): P9-f61c was deferred by F6.1 to F6.2, as F6.2's own instance note above still says; F6.2 carried it forward to this PR with no carry entry recording that hop, which is the gap this note closes. Instances in this PR beyond its findings: P9-f61c (P9, www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js, found by F6.1): a deferred tap-target candidate found while fixing F6.1's four instances, a candidate like P9-rca4 that needs a fix design, deferred by F6.1 to this PR; probe the P9 barrier's grid (handoff/r9-rca-p9@4f3b9d4f), target rule at 51a2e98a86. Class sweeps (Phase D, final): P9: N 11 (judge 4, sweep 5, RCA fold 11), rca yes, sweep S5 at 51a2e98a86, enumerator tools/audit/round9/D14/sweep/P9/enumerate.mjs, seams 5 instance, 1 not applicable, all listed in tools/audit/round9/D14/sweep/S5.json. groups.brief: Round-9 endgame PR EG-B5 (lane EG, architecture: DHW planner extraction, opted in). Added by the endgame review (the ALT endgame plan on the handoff/audit-r9-alt branch); the lane owns no file until its after-edges merge, then borrows what its scope names. Issue #1743 (Fixes). The design spec is the EG-B5 design spec on the handoff/audit-r9-alt branch; this brief is its summary and the spec wins where they differ. Move the nineteen DHW planner core methods of HeatPumpOptimizer in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py (from _dhw_planning_prices and _baseline_dhw_economics through _build_dhw_requirements, _plan_dhw_min_cost, _repair_dhw_floor, _clamp_dhw_to_capacity, _apply_dhw_min_run and _plan_dhw_cheapest_first) into one planner class in a new module, built once per solve in optimize from explicit inputs (the model, the PV export price, the per-solve surplus and price-known mask) and passed down; it writes no attribute. _optimize_with_dhw, _solve_space and _co_optimize stay on the optimizer as orchestration: moving them would need a back-reference, the shape docs/HANDOVER.md refuses. _build_dhw_requirements returns the plan and the requirement; the optimizer keeps _dhw_requirement, assigned where the stash was written (last-writer-wins preserved), and _dhw_legionella_step is deleted (tests read it through a spy on the last build). DhwPlan keeps exactly its published fields: tests/features.py pins them. Shared helpers move without a cycle: _step_humidity and _mean_humidity to custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py, _pin_is_free to custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manual_plan.py; the horizon parameter is typed by a Protocol in the new module, never by a TYPE_CHECKING import, which would add an equivalent guard today's count ratchet refuses. Tests: retarget the direct calls, class-level monkeypatches and captures in tests/features.py and the call in tests/guard_pins.py, with no delegating shims; add the new module to _P3_FILES in tests/features.py or the humidity rule silently stops covering the moved code. Ledger: re-key the moved rows (the planner's, the module constant's and the two humidity helpers') by path, scope and directory with their digests unchanged; tests/mutation_table.py --normalize does not do it; carry the survivor-triage row as it is. Closures: the new module makes the gate FULL; wait for the closures-autofix commit. Null controls: tests/env_drift.py --all byte-identical at the merge base, a whole-file provenance comparison under a stated substitution table, an AST check that the planner writes no attribute, and a three-dot diff at every merge from main (plan principle 3). Preconditions: R9-F10.3 carries #1748 (moved, not added), R9-EG-B8 has fixed #1747, and R9-EG-B5a has landed. Structure-budget writer: never in flight with R9-EG-B5a, R9-EG-B1 or R9-EG-B7. Carried from R9-EG-B8 (#1747; finding-propagation.md): _co_optimize's replan now passes blocked=h.dhw_blocked into _build_dhw_requirements, the same block the first build receives, and the only keyword the two builds may differ in is space_demand. When this PR turns that call into a planner call, the replan keeps the block: the features.py check "a DHW-blocked plan ships no hot water when mostly negative prices tempt the co-optimisation replan (#1747)" and its companion "and every DHW build that solve made was told the mode is blocked" pin it (wood_coil, prices -2.0: 9.22 kWh shipped without the block, 0 with it; re-measure at your merge base). The class is a second call site omitting a defaulted keyword the first passes; EG-B8's PR body carries the AST enumerator it ran (10 seams at its head, each dispositioned): run it on the new module and on optimizer.py after the move. Carried from R9-RCA-1747 (#1747; in-tree copy carry-1743.json, second carry, on handoff/rca-1747 at c04fb2e2): the spy behind "and every DHW build that solve made was told the mode is blocked" patches HeatPumpOptimizer._build_dhw_requirements, and it passes with one build seen. Point the spy at the callable the planner uses for both builds and keep a reach clause (the replan's build is among the builds it saw); R9-F1.11 carries the same clause and may have landed it first. The defect: mutation-nightly and mutation-ledger both run tests/mutation_table.py --scope full --max 40 --jobs 3 under a 330-minute job timeout, and the cost of one mutant is set by the drivers it needs, chiefly tests/features.py. The review measured, over the twenty scheduled runs to 2026-10-03, the nightly's drive step rising from 36 to 285 minutes (peak 2026-10-02, 86 percent of the timeout) while the features.py baseline grew from 95 s to 701 s (833 s in the 2026-10-03 mutation-ledger run); step time does not track the survivor count (correlation -0.05) but tracks the date (0.72). A fixed --max therefore crosses 330 on the first heavy night, losing the measurement and reddening nightly-status, and mutation-ledger, sized the same, may never reach the green night R9-F10.13 waits on. Re-measure all of this at your merge base; carry none of it. (A) A time budget. Give tests/mutation_table.py a wall-clock budget for the mutant phase (drive_pool): once starting another mutant would overrun it at the costs the baseline lines measured, stop starting mutants, name every one not started as not run for the budget, and compute the survivor cap over the mutants evaluated. A run that evaluated none is a refusal, never a pass, so a budget cannot read as a measurement of nothing. Under --drain an unstarted site stays unpinned and untouched, for a later night. Pass a budget under each caller's timeout: mutation-nightly and mutation-ledger in .github/workflows/tests.yml, and the pull request step "Measure pins for the sites this diff added unpinned" under its 60-minute step timeout, which on #1874 began 30 sites and timed out with none pinned (this absorbs the pin-step sizing the pre-study proposed separately). (B) A driver timeout that is not a kill. run_script returns TIMEOUT_RC when a driver overruns --timeout (default 1200 s), and failing_count counts that as one failing check, so killed reads a timeout as a kill, and under --drain that kill becomes a killed_by pin. While tests/features.py grows toward the limit, a mutant that only slows it is pinned as killed. Scale each driver's timeout from its own measured baseline seconds (keep the fixed floor) so growth never turns into kills, while a genuine hang still kills. Demonstration (.claude/rules/defect-root-cause.md, a detector must be shown to detect): (A) a run with a budget too small for its pool evaluates fewer mutants, names the rest, and exits as the cap over the evaluated ones; a budget that admits no mutant refuses; (B) a planted driver that sleeps past the old fixed timeout on a mutant, within the scaled one, is not a kill, and one that never returns still is.
